A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOTA research work. All 13 pages of each version are readable, including the figures, tables, equations, Appendix A experimental details, and Appendix B proof.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original HOTA benchmark results, scalability experiments, opinion-depolarization simulations, and ablations in Section 5, Tables 1–2, and Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains the original HOTA benchmark, scalability, opinion-depolarization, and ablation results in Section 5, Tables 1–2, and Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same objectives, replay buffer, EMA target model, adaptive gradient balancing, and trajectory-generation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Stunnel, Vneck, GMM, BabyMaze, Slit, Box, Sphere with varying smoothness and dimensionality, and 1000-dimensional opinion depolarization. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains NLSB and GSBM for Stunnel/Vneck/GMM, and NLSB, NLOT, and GSBM for BabyMaze/Slit/Box. The opinion-depolarization comparison retains DeepGSB and GSBM.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same evaluation metrics, distributions, model configurations, and experimental settings, including 70,000 training iterations, batch size 1024, and 30 control steps.

E4.justification: The replay-buffer and gradient-balancing ablations in Table 2, coefficient-sensitivity analyses in Figure 4, and Sphere smoothness/dimensionality analyses in Figure 2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report HOTA means and standard deviations across five seeds in Table 1. The plotted uncertainty bands and statistical reporting practices are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–4 retain the same results. For example, HOTA's GMM feasibility remains 0.19 ± 0.05, and its opinion-depolarization objective in Figure 3 remains 460.4 under the same settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 1, coercivity discussion, and Appendix B duality and dynamic-programming proof are unchanged. Equations (1)–(34) differ only in typesetting or extraction spacing.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the density-free HJB/Kantorovich formulation, support for non-smooth costs, scalability, and superior feasibility and optimality.

C2.justification: The interpretations of trajectory separation and ablation tradeoffs remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning Fourier time encoding and the suitability of a simple MLP architecture.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A retain the same network and optimizer details, hyperparameters, RTX 3090 hardware, training-time statement, and baseline code-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to diffusion/matching methods, generalized Schrödinger bridges, and stochastic optimal control.

P1.justification: Author affiliations change from AIRI/MIPT/Skoltech to CILAB.AI, with corresponding email-address and institutional-footnote updates. The scientific prose, terminology, and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The institutional footnotes decrease from three to one, moving two introduction lines from page 2 to page 1 and slightly reflowing the opening pages. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–3 retain their graphics, structure, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The revision updates affiliations and contact details and makes minor layout adjustments. The scientific content, supporting results, limitations, and reproducibility information—including both appendices—remain unchanged, with no meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
